title: Ordering Single Cells and Single Embryos in 3D Confinement: A New Device for High Content Screening
protocol: Heat a 3’’ silicon wafer up to 200 °C to evaporate any presence of humidity.
Spin-coat a thin layer of SU-8 photoresist.
Pre-bake the wafer at 65 °C for 1 min.
Pre-bake the wafer at 95 °C for 3 min.
Load the wafer on the mask aligner for UV exposure.
Place the photolithography mask on it.
Check the power of the UV lamp prior to exposure and optimize the exposure time accordingly.
Irradiate (wavelength = 365 nm) for 41.5 sec (or the optimized exposure time) at 250 mJ/cm².
Protect the eyes from UV light with appropriate safety glasses.
Remove gently the mask from the photoresist layer.
Post-bake the wafer at 65 °C for 1 min.
Post-bake the wafer at 95 °C for 3 min.
Cool the wafer to room temperature on the bench for around 1 min.
Place the wafer in the spin-coater and drop few mm of SU-8 developer to cover the whole wafer area.
Develop for 2 min.
Spin-coat at 1,000 rpm for 30 sec.
Repeat the procedure three times.
Rinse with 2-propanol to ensure the complete removal of undeveloped SU-8.
Hard-bake the wafer at 200 °C to ensure robustness of the fabricated microstructures.
Store the 3’’ wafer with microstructures inside a 94 mm x 15 mm polystyrene Petri dish.
Thoroughly mix in a 1:10 ratio (w/w) the cross-linker and the pre-polymer for a total of 30 g inside a 50 ml tube.
Centrifuge the tube at 1,800 x g for 5 min to remove air bubbles.
Drop gently the PDMS on top of the microstructures.
Place the activated PDMS stamp upside up in a Petri dish next to a 15 ml tube cap.
Fill the cap with 200 µl of Trimethylchlorosilane (TMCS).
Close the Petri dish and let the stamp silanize for 7 min.
Spin-coat the PDMS stamp at 1,500 rpm for 30 sec to deposit a thin layer of liquid PDMS on top of the structures.
Place the spin-coated PDMS stamp in the oven at 65 °C for 4 hr to cure the deposited layer.
Activate the thin PDMS layer by placing the PDMS stamp upside up with a glass coverslip using oxygen plasma cleaner for 30 sec.
Press gently all around the surface of the stamp with tweezers to make the ‘bonding’.
Keep a constant pressure on top of the stamp for around 10 sec.
Gently peel the stamp out of the coverslip after 30 min.
Rinse thoroughly with ethanol and dry.
Glue a small piece (handle) of cured PDMS at the edge of the coverslip with a drop of liquid PDMS and cure as before.
Hydrophilize the 25 mm diameter glass coverslips #0 oxygen plasma treatment at 15 W for 30 sec.
Spin-coat a small drop of PDMS (1:10 w/w cross-linker:pre-polymer) onto the glass coverslips.
Spin-coat at 1,500 rpm for 30 sec for a final thickness of around 50 μm.
Glue a small piece (handle) of cured PDMS of 1 mm x 1 mm x 3 mm in volume at the edge of the coverslip with a small drop of liquid PDMS and cure the PDMS as before.
Store temporarily the PDMS-coated coverslips onto a clean wipe inside a Petri dish to protect from dust deposition.
Put a drop of silanizing reagent on top of each stamp and let it evaporate for 1-2 min.
Dry them under a stream of N2.
Drop the silanized stamp very gently on top of the PDMS-spin-coated glass coverslip stored in the Petri dish.
Ensure both sides are completely parallel during contact.
Place the Petri dish with samples in the vacuum for 1-2 hours to remove air bubbles.
Place the samples in the oven at 65 °C for 4 hours.
Gently peel off the stamp to reveal ‘eggcups’.
Rinse the eggcups thoroughly with ethanol and dry them.
Hydrophilize the ‘eggcups’ in the oxygen plasma cleaner for 30 seconds.
Prepare a solution of fibronectin at 20 µg/ml in PBS.
Sterilize the 'eggcups' with UV light for 5 minutes.
Deposit a small drop (around 20-50 μl) of fibronectin solution to cover the entire 'eggcups' area and incubate for 1 hour at room temperature.
Rinse the ‘eggcups’ gently with PBS, repeating three times.
Use UV-sterilized items or sterilize them prior to use.
Fabricate a cylindrical custom-made plastic piece with dimensions of 63 mm in height, 26 mm external radius, and 7 mm internal radius for a 50 ml tube.
Place 13 ml of cell culture medium inside the tube to ensure at least 2 cm above the cylindrical piece is filled with medium.
Introduce ‘eggcups’ gently into the tube parallel to the upper side of the plastic piece using sharp tweezers.
Hold the sample using PDMS handle and press gently until it lies on top of the upper side of the plastic piece, ensuring full immersion.
Culture cells until 80-100% confluence in a P60 Petri dish.
Collect cells by trypsinization.
Avoid formation of cell aggregates by pipetting up and down thoroughly after trypsinization.
Re-suspend cells into 5 ml culture medium.
Pipette 200 µl of cells on top of the ‘eggcups’.
Centrifuge at 1,800 x g for 2 min.
Check in a microscope the filling percentage of the ‘eggcups’.
If necessary, pipette again 200 µl of cells on top of the ‘eggcups’ and centrifuge.
Repeat the process until reaching the desired filling percentage.
Remove the sample from the tube using sharp tweezers holding the PDMS handle carefully.
Place the sample in a Petri dish with medium.
Rinse to remove excess cells not in the ‘eggcups’ by pipetting up and down gently next to each side of the microstructure array.
Replace the medium with fresh medium to remove nonattached cells.
Place ‘eggcups’ into a microscope holder.
Fill the holder with 1 ml of 10 % FCS L-15 observation medium.
Select the 60X oil objective.
Prepare 3% paraformaldehyde (PFA) and warm at 37 °C.
Remove the ‘eggcups’ sample from the 50 ml tube or microscope holder and place it inside a P35 Petri dish.
Rinse once with PBS 1x.
Remove completely the PBS and drop 1 ml of 3% PFA, incubate for 17 min.
Remove the PFA and rinse twice with 1 ml of PBS 1X.
Permeabilize cells using 1 ml of 0.5% Triton for 3 min.
Wash cells twice with PBS 1x for 5 min.
Incubate cells for Golgi apparatus staining with primary antibody rabbit polyclonal anti-Giantin in a 1:500 dilution in PBS, upside down for 45 min.
Release carefully the ‘Eggcups’ and place them into a P35 Petri dish.
Rinse cells 3 times, 5 min each, with PBS 1x.
Prepare a cocktail in PBS with the secondary antibody Cy3 goat anti-rabbit (1:1,000) and Phalloidin Alexa Fluor 488 (1:200).
Incubate cells with a 100 µl drop of antibody solution onto a plastic film sheet.
Place ‘eggcups’ upside down for 45 min.
Release carefully the ‘eggcups’ and place them into a P35 Petri dish.
Rinse cells 3 times, 5 min each, with PBS 1x.
Incubate cells for nucleus staining placing a 100 µl drop of 1 µg ml-1 DAPI in PBS onto a plastic film sheet.
Place ‘eggcups’ upside down for 45 min.
Release carefully the ‘eggcups’ and place them into a P35 Petri dish.
Rinse cells 3 times, 5 min each, with PBS 1x.
Mount cells using a 15 µl Glycerol:PBS (1:1 v/v) on a standard microscope glass slide.
Seal the sample with nail polish to avoid drying.
Select the 25X or 63X water objective.
Place the fixed sample with the 'eggcups' and focus carefully using brightfield light (phase contrast or DIC) until the 'eggcups' and cells are in the plane of observation.
Open the software and adjust the parameters.
Select the filters GFP, Cy3 and DAPI for actin, Golgi and nucleus observation, respectively; adjust the exposition time for all channels.
Select and focus the region of interest; start image capture.
Prepare the ‘eggcups’ surface as described above.
Culture yeast cells in the proper culture media until reaching an optical density (OD) in the range of 0.2 and 0.8.
Sonicate the culture of yeast cells to remove aggregates.
Insert yeast cells in ‘eggcups’ by centrifugation.
Add 4 ml of cultured cells with appropriate OD onto the tube containing ‘eggcups’.
Centrifuge the tube and gently shake to re-suspend un-deposited cells without disturbing those in ‘eggcups’.
Repeat the centrifugation step twice more.
Rinse yeast cells with the same medium until floating cells are removed efficiently, avoiding disturbance of cells within ‘egggups’.
Place ‘eggcups’ in a microscope holder and fill with filter-sterilized medium for imaging.
Select the 100X oil objective and focus carefully.
Open the software and adjust parameters.
For fission yeast, select GFP and TxRed filters for actin and myosin respectively.
Adjust exposure time for both channels accordingly.
Prepare the ‘eggcups’ surface as described and 25 µm in diameter.
Culture C. elegans embryos in proper culture media.
Insert embryos into ‘eggcups’ by centrifugation using ultrapure water as culture medium.
Rinse the sample as described.
Place the ‘eggcups’ into a microscope holder.
Select the 40X air objective and focus carefully.
Open the software and adjust parameters.
Select an acquisition rate of 3 sec.
